title: [BUG] GithubSearchTool unable to access private repositories
body: ### Description The built-in [`GithubSearchTool`](https://docs.crewai.com/en/tools/search-research/githubsearchtool) from the [`crewai-tools`](https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/tree/main/lib/crewai-tools) library currently appears to be restricted to searching public GitHub repositories. When attempting to use the tool with an authenticated Personal Access Token (PAT) that has the necessary scopes for private access (e.g., the repo scope), the agent receives a resource not found error when targeting private repositories. ### Steps to Reproduce ```python from crewai import Agent, Task, Crew, Process from crewai_tools import GithubSearchTool github_tool = GithubSearchTool( github_repo="/", gh_token="", content_types=["code", "repo"], ) github_researcher = Agent( role='Private Repo File Lister', goal='List all files and their paths found by the GithubSearchTool, strictly reporting only the output of the tool.', backstory=( 'An expert in using the GithubSearchTool. ' 'Its sole focus is to execute the tool and provide the raw, ' 'unprocessed results directly to the user, avoiding any inference or commentary.' ), tools=[github_tool], verbose=True ) github_search_task = Task( description=( "1. Execute the 'GithubSearchTool' with the query 'list all files' " "to retrieve a list of files and their paths from the configured private repository." "2. **CRITICALLY:** Your final answer must be a direct, unedited list of the " "file names and paths returned by the tool. Do not add introductory " "text, analysis, or any files not explicitly found by the tool." ), agent= github_researcher ) crew = Crew( agents=[github_researcher], tasks=[github_search_task], process=Process.sequential ) result = crew.kickoff() print(result) ``` ### Expected behavior The agent successfully authenticates, searches the private repository, and returns the relevant list of files. ### Screenshots/Code snippets ### Operating System Other (specify in additional context) ### Python Version 3.12 ### crewAI Version 1.7.0 ### crewAI Tools Version 1.7.0 ### Virtual Environment Venv ### Evidence ### Possible Solution I have resolved this issue by ensuring that the [`CrewAIRagAdapter`](https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/blob/main/lib/crewai-tools/src/crewai_tools/adapters/crewai_rag_adapter.py) correctly passes all keyword arguments (`kwargs`) to the underlying data loaders. This fix ensures authentication parameters like `gh_token` are utilized, and it should prevent similar configuration bugs with other tools. I will be opening a [Pull Request](#4090) promptly with this solution. ### Additional context **Operating System**: `macOS Sequoia`

linked_prs.title: Forward kwargs to loader calls in CrewAIRagAdapter
linked_prs.patch:
diff --git a/lib/crewai-tools/src/crewai_tools/adapters/crewai_rag_adapter.py b/lib/crewai-tools/src/crewai_tools/adapters/crewai_rag_adapter.py
index b89212de25..be2039c51d 100644
--- a/lib/crewai-tools/src/crewai_tools/adapters/crewai_rag_adapter.py
+++ b/lib/crewai-tools/src/crewai_tools/adapters/crewai_rag_adapter.py
@@ -268,7 +268,9 @@ def add(self, *args: ContentItem, **kwargs: Unpack[AddDocumentParams]) -> None:
                             file_chunker = file_data_type.get_chunker()
 
                             file_source = SourceContent(file_path)
-                            file_result: LoaderResult = file_loader.load(file_source)
+                            file_result: LoaderResult = file_loader.load(
+                                file_source, **kwargs
+                            )
 
                             file_chunks = file_chunker.chunk(file_result.content)
 
@@ -319,7 +321,7 @@ def add(self, *args: ContentItem, **kwargs: Unpack[AddDocumentParams]) -> None:
                 loader = data_type.get_loader()
                 chunker = data_type.get_chunker()
 
-                loader_result: LoaderResult = loader.load(source_content)
+                loader_result: LoaderResult = loader.load(source_content, **kwargs)
 
                 chunks = chunker.chunk(loader_result.content)
